title: Canonical parser front end
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a finite Turing machine $C$ over the Boolean alphabet, an entry state $e$ of $C$, an injective map $q$ from Boolean verdicts to states of $C$, and a natural number $a$, with at least four work tapes. For every Boolean word $x$, the run from state $e$ on input $x$, with all work tapes blank, all work-tape heads at cell zero, and empty output, reaches state $q(v)$ after some time $t\le a(|x|+1)$, for a verdict $v$; no state $q(u)$ is reached at any time $u<t$. The output remains empty at time $t$. If $v$ is false, decoding $x$ in format $F$ gives its fallback code. If $v$ is true, there are bit strings $b,r$ such that pair decoding of $x$ yields $(b,r)$, $b$ is the canonical binary representation of the natural number it encodes, and $r$ has length at least $\max\{F.\mathrm{guard},(4C.k+5)3^{C.k+1}\}$ times one more than that number. At time $t$ the input head is at position $2|b|+3$, and on every work tape other than tape $1$, the tape contents store the canonical ready word determined by $b$ and the tape head is at cell zero.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine $C$ over the Boolean alphabet
An entry state $e$ and an injective map from Boolean verdicts to states
At least four work tapes: $4\le C.k$
No verdict state is reached at any earlier time
The output at time $t$ is empty
False verdict implies decoding gives the fallback code
True verdict implies a pair decode $(b,r)$, canonical binary header, sufficient suffix length, input-head position, and the specified contents and head positions on all work tapes except tape $1$
